title: Agent Lightning: Lightweight RL agent-training framework
gist: Microsoft Research Asia open-sourced Agent Lightning v1.0, a roughly 3,500-line RL framework that trains agents using their real deployment harness via an LLM proxy, runs rollouts as Kubernetes jobs, and lifted Qwen3.5-9B on SWE-bench Verified from 41.8% to 56.4% with about 6,000 samples.

insights.claim: Traditional agentic RL requires reimplementing the agent inside the training framework, which is costly and means the trained agent is not quite the agent that gets deployed; Harnessed Agentic RL has the deployment harness participate directly in RL training.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Removes a major friction in training production agents, favoring frameworks that wrap existing harnesses.
insights.locator: The limits of traditional agentic RL

insights.claim: Agent Lightning places an OpenAI-compatible LLM proxy between agent and model so existing harness code stays unchanged; pointing the model endpoint at the proxy is usually enough to connect to RL training.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Low-integration-cost RL for coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands and OpenCode harnesses.
insights.locator: Building a complete agent RL control plane

insights.claim: Real coding-agent harnesses such as mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, OpenCode, Claude Code and Codex each have their own context management, tool protocols and dependencies, which makes rebuilding them for training expensive and risky for behavioural drift.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Agent value increasingly lives in the harness, not only the model.
insights.locator: Real harnesses have outgrown that assumption

insights.claim: Training with real harnesses raises four challenges: retokenization and sample merging, rollout-level advantage calculation, loss normalization and training-backend scheduling for variable workloads on fixed GPU resources.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Checklist of engineering pitfalls for agent RL.
insights.locator: Four challenges in training with real harnesses

insights.claim: Computing baselines and advantages at the sample level counts rollouts that produce more samples repeatedly, and averaging loss by sample count overweights them; rollout-level advantage and normalization gave higher validation reward and more stable policy entropy.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Evidence that rollout-level statistics matter for stability in agent RL.

insights.claim: Passing harness text through the chat template and tokenizer again can shift token boundaries, so adjacent calls cannot always be merged into one training sample.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: A subtle source of train-inference mismatch in agent RL.

insights.claim: Agent Lightning v1.0 is about 3,500 lines of code with three components: API Gateway, Rollout Controller and a Customized Trainer built on verl.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Small codebase eases adoption and modification by labs and enterprises.
insights.locator: Building a complete agent RL control plane in 3,500 lines of code

insights.claim: Collocated Async RL lets rollout and model updates share the same GPUs and achieved about a 2x end-to-end speedup over synchronous RL while using fewer GPUs than conventional asynchronous RL.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Cuts GPU needs for agent RL, relevant to training cost.

insights.claim: Running rollouts as standard Kubernetes jobs avoids commercial sandbox services such as Modal Sandbox or E2B, where cost climbs quickly with scale, and reuses existing self-managed, cloud or local clusters.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Pressure on paid agent-sandbox vendors as open frameworks go Kubernetes-native.

insights.claim: An end-to-end pipeline on SWE-smith, mini-SWE-agent and Qwen3.5-9B, with reward-hacking safeguards, raised SWE-bench Verified Pass@1 from 41.8% to 56.4% (+14.6 points) with RL alone, using only about 6,000 training samples.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Small open model gains substantially from modest RL data, supporting cheap domain-specialist agent training.
insights.quote: an absolute gain of 14.6 percentage points, using only about 6,000 training samples
